storyline.label: Reinforcement Learning
storyline.latest_title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?

prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of agentic-RL papers, not one developing story. Since Oct 19 it has gathered research-state search training, memory-skill learning, and a study of when fine-grained credit assignment helps or hurts.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Nov 3: MDSKILL, an arXiv paper, internalizes skill memory into agent weights through multi-view on-policy self-distillation, complementing RL for self-evolving agents.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agent RL is shifting from prompt-held memory toward training signals: MDSKILL distills skill memory into the policy, and the Oct 26 credit-assignment study warns finer signals do not always help. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence.

status.detail: A loose set of agentic-RL papers; the newest moves skill memory from the prompt into the model via self-distillation.

beats.headline: ClueFlow trains long-horizon search on attributed research-state transitions
Lifelong agents learn memory and skills bidirectionally within a bounded context
Fine-grained credit assignment can help or hurt multimodal agents
beats.summary: Tested on video editing; finer credit is not automatically better.

beats.headline: CausalXRL explains RL decisions through causal graph reasoning
MDSKILL internalizes skill memory through multi-view self-distillation

open_questions: Does MDSKILL's internalized skill memory beat prompt-held skill memory on agent benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does ClueFlow's attributed research-state training carry to search agents outside the paper's benchmarks?
Do the credit-assignment findings from video editing hold on text-only tool-use agents?
Does bidirectional memory-skill learning stay stable over long interaction histories?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you keep skill memory in prompts, rerun your evals against a distilled variant before committing, and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat all of these results as unreplicated.
